title: Babel and the Nations, part 2 of 2: the tower of Babel; from Shem to Abram
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The early world after the great flood, the wide river plains of the ancient Near East: people dressed in simple garments of rough wool, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

TERAH.name: Terah
TERAH.desc: Terah, a tall, gaunt old man who looks about eighty, with warm brown deeply lined skin, a bald crown with long white hair falling behind his ears to his shoulders, a long white beard, heavy white brows and tired dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of dark brown wool and a wool mantle woven in broad tan and brown stripes over both shoulders, and simple leather sandals

ABRAM.name: Abram
ABRAM.desc: Abram, a tall, strong, upright man who looks about sixty, with warm brown weathered skin, thick wavy dark hair heavily streaked with grey reaching his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SARAI.name: Sarai
SARAI.desc: Sarai, a strikingly beautiful, graceful woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, large dark eyes, high cheekbones and long wavy black hair with a few silver threads, her hair mostly covered by a long indigo-blue wool head shawl that falls over her shoulders, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of undyed cream wool with a woven belt of red and blue, and simple leather sandals

LOT.name: Lot
LOT.desc: Lot, Abram's nephew, a slim young man of about twenty-five with warm brown skin, curly dark-brown hair to his ears, a short sparse dark beard and quick, lively eyes, wearing a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of olive-green wool with a leather belt and a tan wool mantle rolled over one shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SHEM.name: Shem
SHEM.desc: Shem, a son of Noah, a lean, thoughtful man of about thirty with warm brown skin, wavy black hair to his jaw and a short neat black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed cream wool with a rope belt, and simple leather sandals

segs.text: Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.
And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
And they said to one another,
Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.
So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.
Come,
they said,
let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.
Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.
And the LORD said,
If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.
Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.
So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.
That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.
This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.
And after he had become the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.
And after he had become the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Shelah was 30 years old, he became the father of Eber.
And after he had become the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Eber was 34 years old, he became the father of Peleg.
And after he had become the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Peleg was 30 years old, he became the father of Reu.
And after he had become the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Reu was 32 years old, he became the father of Serug.
And after he had become the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Serug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahor.
And after he had become the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.
And after he had become the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran became the father of Lot.
During his father Terah’s lifetime, Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah; she was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.
But Sarai was barren; she had no children.

And Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai the wife of Abram, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan. But when they arrived in Haran, they settled there.
Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.

The whole world had one language: night on an open plain, a great crowd of {FOLK}, of every age, seated in a wide ring around one huge bonfire; a grey-bearded man stands by the fire telling a story with both arms lifted, and every face in the ring is turned to him, laughing at the same moment. Wide view.

A common form of speech: at a stone-ringed well in dry grassland at morning, two travellers who have never met, one a shepherd in a brown wool tunic with a crook and the other a woman in a grey wool dress with a clay water jar, greet each other and talk easily, both smiling, he pointing the way along the road. {TWO}. Medium view.

People journeying eastward: seen from behind, a long column of {FOLK}, with children, flocks of sheep and goats and laden grey donkeys, walks away from us across rolling dry hills straight toward the sun rising low on the horizon ahead of them, their long shadows stretching back toward the viewer. Seen from behind, walking away toward the sunrise. {NOCRANES}. Very wide view.

They found a plain in the land of Shinar: seen from behind, three men and a woman in rough wool stand on the last low ridge with their walking staffs and look out over {SHINAR}, that opens below them, golden in morning light; one man points down at it. Exactly four people, all seen from behind. No buildings anywhere on the plain. Very wide view over their shoulders.

And they settled there: on the bank of a broad reed-fringed river on a flat plain, families of {FOLK}, raise {TENTS}: two men haul a dark tent cloth over its poles, a woman drives a wooden peg with a stone, children carry bundles of cut reeds, and unloaded donkeys drink at the water. No brick buildings. Medium-wide view.

They said to one another, Come, let us make bricks: on a muddy riverbank, a strong bearded man in a brown wool tunic, crouching, holds up a squared lump of wet grey clay in both hands and calls over his shoulder, and four other men and women in rough wool hurry toward him across the mud, one already kneeling to dig clay with his hands. Medium view.

Making bricks: a wide brickfield on a river plain where dozens of {FOLK}, kneel in rows pressing wet clay into small open wooden frames and tipping out the bricks, and behind them thousands of pale mud bricks lie drying in long straight rows that run away toward the horizon under a hot sun. {NOCRANES}. Wide view.

Bake them thoroughly: night, {KILNS}; sweating men in rough wool kilts and tunics feed bundles of reeds into the stoke-holes and one man draws out a glowing red-hot brick on a long wooden paddle, firelight on their faces and arms. Medium view.

Brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar: close view of a mason's two strong hands setting a reddish-brown baked brick down onto a thick bed of glistening black tar on top of a brick wall, black tar squeezing out along the joint, a wooden spreading-stick lying beside it. {HANDS}. No stone anywhere. Close view.

Tar: at the edge of a natural pool of thick black tar that seeps from the ground on a dry plain, three men in rough wool tunics ladle the glistening black tar with long wooden scoops into large clay jars, and a fourth walks away carrying two jars on a shoulder pole toward far-off brick walls. Exactly four men. Medium-wide view.

Come, let us build for ourselves a city: a broad-chested, black-bearded man in a brown wool tunic stands high on a great stack of baked bricks with one arm flung up toward the sky, shouting to a huge crowd of {FOLK}, that fills the ground below him, their arms raised and their faces eager. Low-angle medium-wide view from within the crowd.

A city: wide high view over {BABEL}, spreading across a flat river plain in bright daylight, its streets swarming with hundreds of small figures carrying baskets of bricks on their backs and jars of tar on poles, kilns smoking at its edge. {NOCRANES}. Wide high view.

A tower that reaches to the heavens: seen from the ground at its foot, looking steeply up, {TOWER}, soars up into bright clouds, with tiny workers climbing its long stairway under loads of bricks and standing on the scaffolding far above. {NOCRANES}. Steep low-angle wide view.

That we may make a name for ourselves: on the highest finished terrace of a huge tower of reddish-brown baked brick, among wooden scaffolding, five men in rough wool tunics stand at the brick edge with chins lifted and fists on their hips or raised in triumph, gazing proudly out over a brick city and a flat plain far below them in golden light. Exactly five men. Medium low-angle view.

And not be scattered over the face of all the earth: seen from behind, a man and a woman in rough wool stand on the edge of a high brick terrace and look out over an immense, empty, featureless plain that runs to a far hazy horizon under a huge sky; she grips his arm and he points back down toward crowded brick houses at the foot of the tower. {TWO}, both seen from behind. Very wide view.

Building the tower: in side view, a long line of bent men and women in rough wool tunics climbs from left to right up a broad stairway of baked brick on the side of a huge brick tower, each carrying a tall basket of reddish-brown bricks on the back held by a strap across the forehead, sweat on their faces, the plain far below behind them. {NOCRANES}. Medium side view.

Then the LORD came down: seen from far above the clouds, {GLORY}, streams down through a great opening in a floor of white cloud, and through the opening, very far below, a flat river plain is visible with a tiny brick city on it and a tower no bigger than a grain of sand. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOPEOPLE}. Very high aerial view looking straight down.

To see the city and the tower: seen from high above, a great shaft of golden-white light falls from the top of the frame across {TOWER}, and the brick city around its foot at dawn, lighting them while the plain around stays in blue shadow; tiny workers go on climbing and building, none of them looking up. {NOLIGHTFIG}. High aerial view.

That the sons of men were building: on wooden scaffolding against a wall of reddish-brown baked brick, three masons in rough wool tunics work in a strong shaft of golden light from above, two spreading black tar and laying bricks, while the third, a young man, has stopped with a brick in his hand and shades his eyes to look up into the light. Exactly three men. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view.

As one people: on a broad brick stairway of a huge tower, a single unbroken chain of men and women in rough wool tunics stands one on each step, passing reddish-brown bricks from hand to hand up the stairs in perfect rhythm, every pair of hands moving together, the chain running from the bottom of the frame to the top. {NOCRANES}. Medium-wide view looking up the stairs.

Speaking the same language: a foreman in a brown wool tunic stands on a brick wall with his hand cupped to his mouth, calling, and below him a team of ten men in rough wool leans back together on one thick rope, all in the same pose at the same instant, hauling a heavy squared timber beam up a ramp of earth. No pulleys, no cranes, no wheels. Medium-wide view.

Nothing they devise will be beyond them: night, {TOWER}, dark against a sky of stars, with hundreds of small torches moving up its stairway and along its scaffolding as work goes on in the dark, and high above it a soft golden-white light glows behind the clouds. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.

Come, let Us go down: seen from below on the ragged, scaffolded top of a huge brick tower, the clouds directly overhead tear open and {GLORY}, floods down over the scaffolding; a sudden wind whips ropes and reed mats, and a few workers in rough wool crouch and shield their eyes with their arms. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Low-angle wide view.

Confuse their language: two masons in rough wool tunics stand face to face beside a half-built wall of reddish-brown brick; the older one, grey-bearded, speaks urgently and jabs a finger at the wall, and the younger one stares back at him with his mouth open and his brow knotted in complete bewilderment, one hand lifted to his ear. {TWOMEN}. Medium close view.

They will not understand one another's speech: on a building site among half-built brick walls, a foreman on a wall shouts and waves both arms, and below him the work has fallen into disorder: two groups of men pull the same rope in opposite directions so that a timber beam hangs crooked, a carrier has dropped his basket of bricks, and workers turn to each other with baffled faces and open hands. No pulleys, no cranes. Wide view.

In a narrow street between houses of reddish-brown baked brick, a young mother in a cream wool dress with a small child on her hip speaks anxiously to an older woman neighbour in a grey wool dress, who answers with her hands spread and a frightened, uncomprehending look; behind them other people argue in doorways with baffled gestures. Medium view.

On the open ground before a half-built brick tower, the great crowd has broken apart into separate small knots of {FOLK}: each knot stands close together talking among themselves with their backs turned to the other knots, and wide strips of empty ground lie between them. Wide high view.

So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth: seen from very high above, a half-built brick city with an unfinished square brick tower stands at the centre of a flat plain, and from it six long thin columns of tiny people with donkeys and flocks walk outward in six different directions like the spokes of a wheel, raising dust, toward every horizon. Very high aerial view.

And they stopped building the city: close view of the top of an unfinished wall of reddish-brown baked brick, where a wooden spreading-stick lies stuck fast in a bed of black tar that has gone hard and dull and dusty, beside one last brick set crooked and a small clay tar pot lying on its side. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view.

The abandoned work: a completely deserted building site. {TOWER}, stands silent and empty under a pale sky, its scaffolding bare, loose ropes and reed mats hanging and swinging, a few bricks fallen at its foot and a flock of dark birds wheeling around its ragged top. The ground around the tower is empty bare earth with dropped baskets and scattered bricks. {NOPEOPLE}: not one human figure on the tower, on the stairway or on the ground, near or far. Wide low-angle view.

That is why it is called Babel: dusk on a flat plain; far away and small, the dark silhouette of a half-built brick city and an unfinished square stepped tower stands on the horizon against a red sky, with no fires and no lights in it, and in the foreground only wind-blown dry grass and an empty rutted track. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.

There the LORD confused the language of the whole world: a family in rough wool walks toward the viewer along a track across a flat plain, leaving behind them an unfinished stepped brick tower that stands small and far away on the horizon at their backs: a father in front leading a laden grey donkey by its rope, a mother with a baby bound on her back, and two children; the mother has turned her head to look back over her shoulder at the far tower behind them. They walk toward us, away from the tower. Exactly four walking people and one baby. Medium-wide front view.

{MAPLOOK}. A wide land of brown plains, two long winding blue rivers, green marshes, grey mountain ranges with snow, yellow deserts and a dark blue sea coast, all in low evening light; near the middle, on the plain between the two rivers, stands one tiny brick tower, and from it many faint dusty trails spread outward in every direction across the whole land. {NOPEOPLE}.

Scattered over the face of all the earth: seen from behind, a small band of men, women and children in rough wool and sheepskin cloaks with two laden donkeys climbs away from us up a stony mountain pass between snow-covered peaks, leaning into a cold wind. Seen from behind, climbing up and away. Wide view.

Scattered over the face of all the earth: seen from behind, a small band of men, women and children in rough wool stands on a rocky headland with their bundles set down, looking out for the first time over a vast blue sea to an empty horizon, waves breaking white on the rocks below and gulls in the wind. No boats, no ships. Seen from behind. Wide view.

Scattered over the face of all the earth: a small band of men, women and children in rough wool with laden grey donkeys walks in single file along the crest of a great golden sand dune in a desert of dunes at sunset, tiny dark figures with long shadows. {NOCRANES}. Very wide view.

{MAPLOOK}. High snow-capped mountains fill the top of the picture, and from them two rivers run down through green foothill valleys and out across a broad tawny plain toward the bottom of the picture, in clear morning light after rain. {NOPEOPLE}. No buildings.

Two years after the flood, Shem became the father of Arphaxad: {SHEM}, standing in a green mountain valley where young saplings and fresh grass grow up among great bleached trunks of old fallen driftwood, holding {INFANT} in the crook of his arm and looking down at the child with quiet joy. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium view.

Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters: {OLDSHEM}, seated on a stone bench under a spreading vine in front of a goat-hair tent, with a crowd of sons, daughters, grandchildren and tiny great-grandchildren of every age in rough wool gathered around him and a small girl climbing onto his knee. Medium-wide view.

{ARPHAXAD}, standing beside a stone-walled sheepfold in a high green valley at sunrise and lifting {INFANT} up before him in both hands, laughing, with sheep pressing at the wall behind him. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium view.

{ARPHAXAD}, now grey-haired and grey-bearded, walking with a staff at the head of his many sons and daughters, who drive flocks of sheep and goats and lead laden donkeys down a winding valley out of the mountains toward a wide plain that opens golden below. Wide view.

{SHELAH}, kneeling on the grassy bank of a broad river at dawn and receiving {INFANT} into his arms from his wife, a young woman with a long black braid in a tan wool dress, who sits on a spread fleece; mist on the water behind them. Exactly one man, one woman and one baby. Medium view.

{SHELAH}, now grey-bearded, guiding a wooden plough drawn by two brown oxen through dark river-bottom soil and showing two of his grown sons how to hold it, while his daughters walk behind scattering seed from baskets and more children watch from the field's edge. Wide view.

{EBER}, seated at night in the doorway of a dark goat-hair tent beside a small clay oil lamp, holding {INFANT} along his forearm and bending his head over the sleeping child, a flock of sheep lying dimly in the starlight behind. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium view.

Eber lived 430 years: {EBER}, now extremely old, his hair and square beard pure white, seated on a fleece at the entrance of the largest tent of a great encampment of dark goat-hair tents that covers the plain, while sons, daughters and descendants of every age come and go around him among flocks and cooking fires. Wide view.

{PELEG}, walking along the grassy bank of a straight irrigation channel between green barley fields on a flat plain, carrying {INFANT} against his shoulder and steadying the child's head with his hand. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium view.

{PELEG}, now grey-haired, standing knee-deep in a newly dug channel on a flat plain with a wooden spade, among his grown sons who dig beside him, as one son breaks the last earth bank and river water rushes foaming into the channel; his daughters carry away earth in baskets. Medium-wide view.

{REU}, standing on a round threshing floor heaped with golden grain at harvest time, holding {INFANT} high against the blue sky and grinning, chaff drifting on the wind around them. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium low-angle view.

{REU}, now white-bearded, seated at the head of a long evening meal laid on woven mats in a walled yard of mud brick, tearing a flat loaf to share, with his many sons and daughters and their children seated along both sides, passing bowls. Wide view.

{SERUG}, kneeling in {URHOUSE}, beside a low cradle woven of reeds in which lies {INFANT}, and letting the baby grip his finger, sunlight slanting across the yard. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium view.

{SERUG}, now grey-bearded, standing at a market stall of bales of raw wool and folded cloth in a busy street of tan mud-brick houses, weighing wool on a hand-held wooden balance while two grown sons carry bales and a daughter folds cloth beside him. No coins. Medium-wide view.

{NAHOR_E}, standing on the flat roof of a tan mud-brick house at dusk, holding {INFANT} wrapped against his chest, with the flat rooftops of a great mud-brick city, palm trees and a broad river spreading out behind him under an orange sky. Exactly one man and one baby. No domes, no arches. Medium view.

Nahor lived 119 years: close view of the thin, wrinkled hand of an old man in a dark blue-grey wool sleeve resting in blessing on the bowed dark-haired head of a grown man who kneels before him, in warm lamplight. Only the old man's hand and forearm and the back of the kneeling man's bowed head and shoulders are seen; no faces. Close view.

Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran: seen from behind, a tall man with greying dark hair in an ankle-length tunic of dark brown wool and a mantle woven in broad tan and brown stripes stands in the doorway of a mud-brick house looking out at three small boys of different ages, about seven, five and three, in little wool tunics, who chase each other around a sunlit courtyard. Exactly one man, seen from behind, and three small boys. Medium-wide view.

The generations from Shem to Abram: a long line of men walking one behind another, each a father followed by his grown son, down a winding track from high blue mountains in the far distance onto a broad river plain in the foreground, dark silhouettes with staffs against a glowing evening sky. Exactly ten men in the line. Very wide view.
{UR}, seen from across the river in warm late-afternoon light, small figures on the bank unloading a reed boat and carrying jars up toward the city gate. Wide view.

This is the account of Terah: in {URHOUSE}, {TERAH}, sits on a low brick bench with his staff across his knees, facing the viewer, and in front of him, seen from behind, stand his three grown sons, three bearded men in ankle-length wool tunics, one russet-red, one blue-grey and one olive-green. Exactly four men; the three sons are seen only from behind. Medium-wide view over the sons' shoulders.

And Haran became the father of Lot: {HARAN_M}, crouching in a sunlit street of tan mud-brick houses with his arms open, as his son, {BOYLOT}, runs laughing into them. Exactly one man and one small boy. Medium view.

During his father Terah's lifetime, Haran died: outside the tan mud-brick walls of a great city at dusk, {TERAH}, kneels alone beside {GRAVE}, newly raised on dry ground, his staff fallen beside him, one hand pressed flat on the stones and his head bowed in grief. {ONE}. No body is seen. Medium-wide view.

In his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans: seen from behind, a tall old man with long white hair in a dark brown tunic and a tan-and-brown striped mantle, leaning on a staff, walks slowly away from a burial mound of stones toward the gate of a great walled mud-brick city, holding the hand of {BOYLOT}, who looks back over his shoulder at the grave. Exactly one old man and one small boy. Wide view from behind.

And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves: a double wedding procession in a street of tan mud-brick houses at evening: seen from behind, two bridegrooms in long wool tunics, one with a russet-red mantle and one with a tan fringed shawl, walk side by side, each leading by the hand a bride wrapped in a long veil, one indigo-blue and one saffron-yellow, that covers her head and face; around them neighbours clap, a woman beats a hand drum and children scatter flower petals. The two couples are seen only from behind. Medium-wide view.

Abram's wife was named Sarai: in {URHOUSE}, in morning light, {SARAI}, kneeling at a stone quern grinding grain, looks up with a warm smile as {ABRAM}, comes in through the wooden door carrying a newborn lamb in his arms. {TWO}. Medium view.

Nahor's wife was named Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of both Milcah and Iscah: at the door of a tan mud-brick house, {NAHOR_B}, takes a clay water jar from the shoulder of his wife, {MILCAH}, while beside her stands her younger sister Iscah, a girl of about sixteen with the same heart-shaped face and curly dark-brown hair, in a plain cream wool dress, holding a smaller jar. Exactly one man and two young women. Medium view.

But Sarai was barren: at a city well in a small square of tan mud-brick houses, {SARAI}, stands holding an empty clay water jar in both hands and watches with quiet longing as, a few steps away, three young mothers in wool dresses sit on the well steps laughing together, each with a baby or small child in her lap. Exactly four women and three small children. Medium-wide view.

She had no children: evening in a quiet lamplit room of a mud-brick house, {ABRAM}, and {SARAI}, sit facing each other on woven mats on either side of a low wooden table set with bread and two clay cups; the room around them is silent and bare, and he reaches across the table and lays his hand over hers. {TWO}. No children. Medium view.
Close view of the face of {SARAI}, in warm lamplight at night, her eyes lowered and bright with unshed tears, her indigo-blue head shawl framing her face. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot and his daughter-in-law Sarai: at dawn four people walk out of the gate of a walled city of tan mud brick toward the viewer with {CARAVAN}. From left to right they are: {LOT}, leading a laden grey donkey by its rope; {TERAH}, in front with his staff; {ABRAM}, with one hand on a second donkey's pack; and {SARAI}, walking beside Abram. Exactly four people: three men and one woman. No camels, no horses, no carts. Medium-wide view.

They set out from Ur of the Chaldeans: seen from behind and high up, {CARAVAN}, with four small figures on foot, travels away from us along a dusty road beside a broad river, leaving behind in the foreground corner the tan mud-brick walls and palm trees of a great city; ahead of them the road and the river run on toward far pale hills at sunrise. Exactly four small figures, seen from behind. No camels, no carts. Very wide high view.

{MAPLOOK}. A broad river winds in great loops across a wide tawny land from the lower right corner, where a tiny walled mud-brick city stands on its bank among green fields, up toward far blue hills at the upper left; a thin dusty track follows the river the whole way, and on it, small as ants, a tiny caravan moves away from the city. {NOPEOPLE} except the tiny caravan.

For the land of Canaan: at an evening camp on a dry rise, beside a small fire and resting donkeys, {ABRAM}, stands gazing out toward the far horizon where the sun is setting, his hand shading his eyes, and beside him {LOT}, crouching to feed the fire, looks up at him and follows his gaze. {TWOMEN}. Medium-wide view.

On the road: fording a wide shallow river in bright daylight, {LOT}, wades knee-deep, leading by its rope a grey donkey on which {SARAI}, rides sideways, one hand gripping the pack; behind them sheep and goats splash through the shallows. {TWO}. Medium-wide view.

But when they arrived in Haran: seen from behind, four dusty travellers on foot with {CARAVAN}, come over a low rise and stop, looking ahead at {HARANTOWN}. Exactly four travellers, seen from behind: an old man with a staff in a striped mantle, a man in a russet-red mantle, a woman in an indigo-blue head shawl and a young man in olive-green. No camels, no carts. Wide view over their shoulders.

They settled there: in front of a tan mud-brick house with a flat roof and an open wooden door, {TERAH}, has sat down heavily on a brick bench beside the door with his staff leaning against the wall and his eyes closed, while behind him {ABRAM}, lifts a heavy bundle down from the back of a grey donkey. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.

Terah lived 205 years: in a dim room of a mud-brick house lit by one clay lamp, {TERAH}, lies on a low bed of fleeces under a striped wool blanket, very frail, his eyes half closed, and {ABRAM}, kneels beside the bed holding his father's hand in both of his. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.

And he died in Haran: on a grassy rise outside a walled mud-brick town at evening, three people stand with bowed heads before {GRAVE}, on which a tall plain wooden staff has been laid. From left to right they are: {LOT}; {ABRAM}; and {SARAI}. Exactly three people: two men and one woman. No body is seen. Medium-wide view.

Seen from behind, a tall man with grey-streaked dark hair in an ankle-length cream wool tunic and a deep russet-red mantle stands alone at dusk on a rise outside a walled mud-brick town, beside a road that runs on across the darkening plain to the far south-western horizon, where a low band of soft golden light glows under the clouds. Exactly one man, seen from behind. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view from behind.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 11:1–32, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 11:1-32 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (as in earlier units), P the people of Babel speaking together (11:3-4, one voice for the crowd).
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

New faces made by this unit, for all of Genesis 12 onward: refs/REF-ABRAM.jpg, REF-SARAI.jpg, REF-LOT.jpg, REF-TERAH.jpg (character keys ABRAM, SARAI, LOT, TERAH; copy the description text word for word). Abram is 75 when he leaves Haran (12:4) and Sarai ten years younger (17:17), yet she is still called very beautiful (12:11, 12:14); with the long lifespans of this chapter they are painted as a vigorous man who looks about sixty and a beautiful woman who looks about forty-five (I). Lot looks about twenty-five (I). Later life stages (Abraham at 99, Sarah at 90) should be new sheets derived from these.

Abram's and Sarai's younger years (11:26-29) are never shown face-on: Terah's three sons are small boys (R1) or grown men seen from behind (S2), and the wedding (U1) is seen from behind with veiled brides, so the faces of the reference sheets appear only at their Genesis 12 age (U2 onward). Nahor (Abram's brother), Milcah, Iscah and Haran have description blocks only (NAHOR_B, MILCAH, HARAN_M); Haran is given Lot's colouring. The order of birth of Terah's sons is not pictured as known.

Babel (11:1-9): the tower is a great square stepped tower of baked brick (I, from the text's brick and tar and from the stepped temple-towers of Mesopotamia); the text says only 'a tower that reaches to the heavens'. It is always unfinished. 'Journeyed eastward' (11:2) follows the BSB wording: the people walk toward the sunrise (the Hebrew can also be read 'from the east'; not resolved beyond the translation). The tar pool (C5) is I. Building scenes use no cranes, pulleys or wheels.

God is light only (GLORY), never a figure. 'The LORD came down' (11:5) is light descending through cloud with the tower tiny below (E1): the text itself has God come down to see the tower that was to reach the heavens. 'Let Us go down' (11:7): the plural is not pictured or explained. How the scattering happened is not described by the text; it is shown as people who can no longer understand each other gathering into separate groups and leaving in different directions (H1, H2 T for the fact, particulars D). The far places in I4-I6 (mountains, sea, desert) are D.

The line of Shem (11:10-26): one picture per verse, the father with his newborn son, then the same man older among his 'other sons and daughters'. Unlike Genesis 5 this list never says 'and then he died', so no graves are shown in it. The settings move from mountain valleys down to the river plain and into mud-brick towns (D; the text gives no places before Ur). Shem at 11:10 uses refs/REF-SHEM.jpg and his description from s01e02b; the other fathers have description blocks only. Whether Babel fell in the days of Peleg (10:25) is not pictured. R2, ten men walking in line, counts Shem to Abram as this chapter lists them (Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, Abram).

Ur of the Chaldeans (11:28, 11:31): its location is disputed (southern Mesopotamia or the north near Haran). Not resolved: it is painted as a great mud-brick city on a broad river with palms, the map view (W3) shows only a river and a road with no coastline, and no direction or distance is asserted. No ziggurat or temple is shown in Ur.

Terah's death (11:32) is told before Abram's departure (12:1-4) and the pictures follow the text's order; the question raised by the ages (70 + 75 against 205; compare Acts 7:4) is not resolved. X3, Abram alone looking down the road toward a far light, is D and hands over to Genesis 12; the light is on the horizon only and nothing is said.
Sarai's barrenness (11:30): shown by the mothers at the well (V1), a quiet childless table (V2) and her face (V3, D). No camels are shown in this unit (the text names none here).
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
